chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: The Kentucky coal-country tent show that split his lip
summary: He lasted two days on a Kentucky tent show, too young for such hard playing, but values the experience young musicians no longer get.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And how did you travel around?

Oh a lot of that stuff I did in Nashville, itself. The only tent show I played wound up in Kentucky. In the coal mines area. But I didn't stay because my lip split wide open. After a couple of days I had to leave, I just went back home. I couldn't play a -- that tent. I was too young and that was for a hard core, that thing -- there was a trumpet player with me on that show he'd been on that show and he had hardened himself to it. But I could never remember this guy's name, but he was expert carnival, that's all he did was play the -- those type of shows. But I couldn't do it I was too young and I wasn't strong enough to play, so I stayed about two days and I had to go back to Nashville, I couldn't take it. But it was good experience though. But not for me.
But all of this was good experience, wasn't it?
Any experience that young musicians today just don't get.

That's right they don't get that, no. And course Nashville being away from everything. That's all they had there, carnivals and medicine shows and minstrel shows. It was just constantly playing in Nashville.
